tasks.specExcerpt:
Goal: Today a pending sentinel's owner is encoded in its filename (`pending/<sid>__<task>`). Six readers hand-copy the parser that splits on the first `__`; two of them (ops-stop-hook.sh, statusline.sh) must stay bash-builtin-only. Decide whether ownership should move into a body field (`owner=<sid>`), and if yes, carry the change through.
1. decide filename-vs-body ownership. The decision must weigh: the six hand-copied readers, the builtin-only constraint, the O_EXCL open in ops-task.sh, the legacy migration in ops-sessionstart-hook.sh, and that an unowned sentinel must keep failing CLOSED. Record the decision and the rejected option in DECISIONS.md.
2. Mechanically apply it [the decision].
NORTH STAR: Sentinel ownership lives where six readers and three writers agree on it, and the Stop gate still blocks on mine + unowned. Missed if: any reader and writer disagree on an owner, or an unowned sentinel stops blocking.
// DECISION (planner): KEEP THE FILENAME. Reasons to record, one per spec criterion: (a) O_EXCL: ops-task.sh creates name+owner in ONE atomic open; a body needs open-then-write, so a reader can see an empty body = unowned (blocks every session) or a truncated sid = foreign (owner's gate opens). (b) ops-adopt.sh/ops-verdict.sh re-stamp by rename (atomic); a body rewrite is not. (c) builtin-only readers: a body means one bounded read + NUL probe per sentinel in statusline's ~300ms budget and in the hook. (d) the body is already UNTRUSTED input (case _"sentinel BODY is untrusted input"_) — moving the owner there lets untrusted bytes decide the gate. (e) migration: a second name->body migration, and during the per-session .operator/bin refresh old CLIs write names new readers ignore = reader/writer disagreement, the North Star's miss condition. (f) the six hand copies do not disappear — they become six body parsers; check_guard_parity already pins the name parsers. Consequence: requirement 2 is a no-op for code; no writer or reader changes.
steps: Branch off main, not the current feat/jev-decide (PR #190 work lives there): `git fetch origin && git checkout -b chore/sentinel-owner-decision origin/main`.

Read the ledger contract: `cat templates/DECISIONS-header.md` (column order + kind enum) and `tail -5 .operator/DECISIONS.md` (live row shape). Confirm the file's path with `ls .operator/DECISIONS.md`; run `git check-ignore -v .operator/DECISIONS.md` to learn whether the row is committed or local-only, and say which in the report.
Pick a kind from validate_plugin.DECISIONS_RECORD_KINDS (run the python one-liner in testCycle). Never a DECISIONS_GATED_KINDS member.

Append exactly one row with a single `printf '...\n' >> .operator/DECISIONS.md` (one write, no editor rewrite of the file — another session has an open task here). Row text: id `sentinel-owner-in-filename`; decision 'ownership stays in pending/<sid>__<task>; rejected: body field owner=<sid>'; reasons (a)-(f) from the excerpt, compressed to one cell; consequence 'no writer/reader change; unowned stays fail-closed'.

Re-run the grep (expect 1) and the kind check. If tracked, `git add .operator/DECISIONS.md` only and commit: `git commit -m 'decision: sentinel ownership stays in the filename (body owner= rejected)'`.

tasks.specExcerpt:
3. Add red-first cases to tests/test-scripts.sh for: owned, unowned (blocks), foreign (reports).
5. Raise FLOOR_SHELL in tests/floors.env by the number of cases added.
CLAUDE.md coupling: ops-stop-hook.sh blocks on mine + unowned and merely reports foreign. Unowned fails CLOSED — keeps pre-0.4 empty sentinels gating. The partition rule lives in ONE file, scripts/lib/partition.sh, sourced by ops-stop-hook.sh (gate) and statusline.sh (bar). FLOOR_* is a FLOOR (>=) over passed+skipped, raised in the SAME commit as the cases. Every skip is a per-CASE skip(). Case titles are `echo "-- Case ..."` lines. A new test proves nothing until it FAILS on the pre-fix code (user rule). Mutation tests need an isolated tree. NORTH STAR: Missed if any reader and writer disagree on an owner, or an unowned sentinel stops blocking.
steps: Baseline first: `bash tests/test-scripts.sh 2>&1 | tail -3` — record passed/failed/skipped and any failing names; `grep FLOOR_SHELL tests/floors.env` — record the value.

Read the existing _"sentinel ownership"_ case and copy its fixture setup (temp project with ops-init.sh, the Stop-hook JSON payload carrying session_id, how it runs statusline.sh). Do NOT invent a payload shape or message string: read the foreign-report text from scripts/ops-stop-hook.sh and the blocking-count text from scripts/statusline.sh and assert on those exact substrings.

Write Case OWNED: in a fresh fixture, `.operator/bin/ops-task.sh t1 --owner SID_A` -> Stop hook with session_id SID_A exits 2; with SID_B exits 0 and reports foreign. Then `.operator/bin/ops-adopt.sh --owner SID_B t1` -> hook as SID_B exits 2, as SID_A exits 0; statusline for SID_B shows t1 as blocking, for SID_A does not. (Writer->reader agreement for both writers and both builtin readers.)
Write Case UNOWNED: `: > .operator/pending/t2` (the pre-0.4 empty, unowned shape) -> hook exits 2 for SID_A AND for SID_B; statusline counts it as blocking for both.
Write Case FOREIGN: `.operator/bin/ops-task.sh t3 --owner SID_B` -> hook as SID_A exits 0 AND its output contains the foreign-report substring; statusline for SID_A does not count t3 as blocking.

Run the suite alone: expect the three new cases GREEN on current code (behavior is unchanged by decision). Now prove red-first in an isolated copy: `rm -rf /tmp/own-mut && cp -R . /tmp/own-mut && cd /tmp/own-mut`. M1: edit scripts/lib/partition.sh so an unowned name lands in the foreign bucket -> only UNOWNED goes red. Re-copy. M2: make sentinel_owner_of_name always yield an empty owner -> OWNED goes red (SID_B is now blocked on SID_A's task). Re-copy. M3: put foreign names in the mine bucket -> FOREIGN goes red. Record each red line; if a case stays green under its mutation, first check the mutation hit (wrong-mutation-proves-nothing), then fix the case.

Back in the repo, run the suite alone again; FLOOR_SHELL += (new passed+skipped) - (baseline passed+skipped). Note: the spec says 'number of cases added', but the floor counts checks, not Case headers — use the measured delta and state both numbers in the commit message.
`shellcheck tests/test-scripts.sh`; `git add tests/test-scripts.sh tests/floors.env`; `git commit -m 'tests: owned/unowned/foreign sentinel round-trip cases, red under M1-M3; FLOOR_SHELL +N'`.

Body: decision — sentinel ownership stays in the filename, body `owner=<sid>` rejected (reasons: atomic O_EXCL open and rename, untrusted body, builtin-only readers, migration skew); no writer/reader change; new owned/unowned/foreign round-trip cases; FLOOR_SHELL raised.
Run the release gate -> exit 0. Run every gate-suite rung (shell rung ALONE) and `shellcheck` on any touched .sh; compare pass counts to the ownership-cases baseline.

`git add .claude-plugin/plugin.json CHANGELOG.md`; `git commit -m 'v0.13.0: sentinel ownership stays in the filename (decision + round-trip cases)'`. Push only with an explicit remote+branch: `git push -u origin chore/sentinel-owner-decision`.
